quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'comfortable'.
quests.explanation: In longer words, one syllable always stands out — find it and give it extra length and volume.
quests.textToSpeak: I usually relax in my comfortable living room.
quests.phoneticHint: Stress lands on the first syllable: COM-fort-able.

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'history'.
quests.explanation: Three-syllable words still have just one stressed beat — locate it and let the others fall away lightly.
quests.textToSpeak: The university offers an interesting history program.
quests.phoneticHint: Stress lands on the first syllable: HIS-to-ry.

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'company' and 'quarterly'.
quests.explanation: Pick out the strongest syllable in the word and lean into it; keep the other two syllables light.
quests.textToSpeak: The company organizes a quarterly performance review.
quests.phoneticHint: First-syllable stress: COM-pa-ny, QUAR-ter-ly. Second-syllable stress: per-FOR-mance.

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'visited' and 'monument'.
quests.explanation: Even in longer words, only one syllable carries the main stress — make that one clearly louder.
quests.textToSpeak: We visited an incredible historical monument.
quests.phoneticHint: Stress lands up front in both: VIS-it-ed, MON-u-ment.

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'family' and 'important'.
quests.explanation: Find the stressed syllable first, then let the unstressed ones shrink in length and volume around it.
quests.textToSpeak: My family celebrates every important anniversary together.
quests.phoneticHint: First-syllable stress: FAM-i-ly, CEL-e-brates, EV-er-y. Second-syllable stress: im-POR-tant, to-GETH-er.

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'department'.
quests.explanation: Longer words still follow the one-stress rule: find the strong syllable and soften the rest.
quests.textToSpeak: The department store offers an incredible discount today.
quests.phoneticHint: Stress lands on the second syllable: de-PART-ment.

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'restaurant' and 'vegetable'.
quests.explanation: Give one syllable real weight and let the surrounding syllables stay quick and unstressed.
quests.textToSpeak: The restaurant serves an unbelievable vegetable curry.
quests.phoneticHint: Stress lands up front in both: RES-tau-rant, VEG-e-ta-ble.

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'develops' and 'computer'.
quests.explanation: Three syllables, one stress: locate the strong beat and let the other syllables fade around it.
quests.textToSpeak: The laboratory develops innovative computer software.
quests.phoneticHint: Stress lands on the middle syllable in both: de-VEL-ops, com-PU-ter.

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'hospital' and 'recommends'.
quests.explanation: Listen for which syllable gets the pitch and volume boost — that's the one to lean into.
quests.textToSpeak: The hospital recommends a particular medication schedule.
quests.phoneticHint: 'Hospital' stresses the first syllable (HOS-pi-tal); 'recommends' stresses the last (rec-om-MENDS).

quests.hint: Find the stressed syllable in 'orchestra' and 'symphony'.
quests.explanation: Even longer words keep a single clear stress point — find it and let everything else stay light.
quests.textToSpeak: The orchestra performed an extraordinary symphony tonight.
quests.phoneticHint: Stress lands up front in both: OR-ches-tra, SYM-pho-ny.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'toothbrush' and 'bedroom'.
quests.explanation: In compound nouns, the first word almost always carries the stress — say it louder than the second.
quests.textToSpeak: I left my toothbrush near the bedroom doorway.
quests.phoneticHint: TOOTH-brush, BED-room, DOOR-way — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'classroom' and 'whiteboard'.
quests.explanation: Compound nouns lean their stress onto the first element; the second part stays comparatively quiet.
quests.textToSpeak: The classroom has a new whiteboard and bookshelf.
quests.phoneticHint: CLASS-room, WHITE-board, BOOK-shelf — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'workplace' and 'timesheet'.
quests.explanation: Give the first part of the compound extra punch, and let the second part trail off more softly.
quests.textToSpeak: The workplace updated the timesheet and the paycheck.
quests.phoneticHint: WORK-place, TIME-sheet, PAY-check — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'timetable' and 'airport'.
quests.explanation: The rule for compound nouns: stress the front word, keep the back word light and unstressed.
quests.textToSpeak: We checked the timetable before the airport pickup.
quests.phoneticHint: TIME-table, AIR-port, PICK-up — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'treehouse' and 'backyard'.
quests.explanation: Two words joined as one noun still stress just the first — make it clearly louder than the second.
quests.textToSpeak: My grandfather built a treehouse in the backyard.
quests.phoneticHint: TREE-house, BACK-yard — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'shopkeeper' and 'toothpaste'.
quests.explanation: Lean the weight onto the first half of the compound; the second half rides along more quietly.
quests.textToSpeak: The shopkeeper restocked the toothpaste and the notebook.
quests.phoneticHint: SHOP-keeper, TOOTH-paste, NOTE-book — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'breadbox' and 'teapot'.
quests.explanation: Compound nouns almost always stress their first piece, leaving the second piece unstressed.
quests.textToSpeak: I bought a breadbox and a teapot for the kitchen.
quests.phoneticHint: BREAD-box, TEA-pot — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'laptop' and 'keyboard'.
quests.explanation: Say the opening word of the compound with more force, then ease off through the second word.
quests.textToSpeak: I charged my laptop near the keyboard and headset.
quests.phoneticHint: LAP-top, KEY-board, HEAD-set — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first part in 'earplugs' and 'first-aid'.
quests.explanation: The first word in a compound noun gets the spotlight; the second stays in its shadow.
quests.textToSpeak: The pharmacy stocks earplugs and a first-aid kit.
quests.phoneticHint: EAR-plugs, FIRST-aid — stress the front part each time.

quests.hint: Stress the first word in 'playground' and 'sandbox'.
quests.explanation: Stress belongs on the first word of a compound noun — the second simply completes the picture.
quests.textToSpeak: The playground has a sandbox near the playhouse.
quests.phoneticHint: PLAY-ground, SAND-box, PLAY-house — stress the front word each time.

quests.hint: Notice how -sion and -tion pull stress in 'decision' and 'vacation'.
quests.explanation: Endings like -tion and -sion pull the stress onto the syllable right before them.
quests.textToSpeak: My decision about the vacation felt comfortable.
quests.phoneticHint: de-CI-sion, va-CA-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'graduation' and 'emotional'.
quests.explanation: When you see -tion or -sion, stress lands on the syllable that comes right before that ending.
quests.textToSpeak: The graduation ceremony felt incredibly emotional.
quests.phoneticHint: grad-u-A-tion, e-MO-tion-al — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'organization' and 'promotion'.
quests.explanation: The suffix -tion doesn't take the stress itself — it pulls it onto the syllable just before it.
quests.textToSpeak: The organization announced a major promotion.
quests.phoneticHint: or-gan-i-ZA-tion, pro-MO-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'destination' and 'preparation'.
quests.explanation: Find the syllable right before -tion or -sion; that's where the stress always lands.
quests.textToSpeak: The destination required careful preparation.
quests.phoneticHint: des-ti-NA-tion, prep-a-RA-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'celebration'.
quests.explanation: These suffixes act like a magnet, drawing the stress onto the syllable directly in front of them.
quests.textToSpeak: Our celebration felt particularly memorable this year.
quests.phoneticHint: cel-e-BRA-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'information' and 'promotion'.
quests.explanation: No matter how long the word, -tion and -sion always pull stress onto the syllable just before them.
quests.textToSpeak: The information about the promotion seemed reliable.
quests.phoneticHint: in-for-MA-tion, pro-MO-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'combination' and 'sensation'.
quests.explanation: The syllable just before -tion or -sion is always the stressed one — the suffix itself stays unstressed.
quests.textToSpeak: The combination of spices created a memorable sensation.
quests.phoneticHint: com-bi-NA-tion, sen-SA-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'application' and 'verification'.
quests.explanation: Look one syllable back from -tion or -sion — that's exactly where the stress belongs.
quests.textToSpeak: The application required a quick verification.
quests.phoneticHint: ap-pli-CA-tion, ver-i-fi-CA-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'medication' and 'consideration'.
quests.explanation: Stress shifts to sit right before -tion or -sion, no matter how the base word was originally stressed.
quests.textToSpeak: The medication required careful consideration.
quests.phoneticHint: med-i-CA-tion, con-sid-er-A-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.

quests.hint: Notice how -tion pulls stress in 'production' and 'reaction'.
quests.explanation: The ending -tion reshapes the whole word's rhythm, always pulling stress just ahead of itself.
quests.textToSpeak: The production received an enthusiastic reaction.
quests.phoneticHint: pro-DUC-tion, re-AC-tion — the stress sits right before the ending.
